title: Herode rege / multis convocatis

authoringPolicy.method: concept → authentic example → recognition → controlled manipulation → liturgical reading → retrieval
authoringPolicy.vocabularyPolicy: Only frozen Lesson 28 vocabulary is introduced; proper names and later terms remain support.
authoringPolicy.authenticTextPolicy: Ablative absolutes are anchored in Vulgate narrative clauses.

sources.sourceLatin: Defuncto autem Herode, ecce angelus Domini apparuit in somnis Joseph in Aegypto.
sources.provenanceNote: Defuncto Herode is a classic ablative absolute giving background circumstance.

sources.sourceLatin: Convocatis autem duodecim Apostolis, dedit illis virtutem et potestatem super omnia daemonia.
sources.provenanceNote: Convocatis Apostolis is an ablative absolute preceding the main action.

sources.sourceLatin: Quod cum cognovissent turbae, secutae sunt illum: et excepit eos, et loquebatur illis de regno Dei.
sources.provenanceNote: turbae is introduced inside a multi-clause narrative immediately adjacent to the ablative-absolute lesson.

sources.sourceLatin: Accedentes autem duodecim dixerunt illi: Dimitte turbas.
sources.provenanceNote: turba recurs in narrative syntax; participial compression is contrasted with ablative absolute.

casePanel.policy: Ablative absolute uses ablative morphology but stands syntactically apart from the main clause.

ablativeAbsoluteFramework.form: Usually noun/pronoun + participle, both ablative; sometimes noun + noun/adjective.
ablativeAbsoluteFramework.function: Compressed background circumstance: when, after, since, although, with... depending on context.
ablativeAbsoluteFramework.diagnostic: The ablative phrase is grammatically independent of the main clause; its noun is not an argument of the main verb.

learningBlocks.title: A whole background clause can collapse into the ablative

learnerCopy.en: An ablative absolute compresses circumstance into an ablative noun/pronoun plus participle. Translate the relation from context: when, after, since, although, with.
learnerCopy.fr: L'ablatif absolu condense une circonstance en nom/pronom à l'ablatif + participe. Le lien se traduit selon le contexte : lorsque, après que, puisque, bien que, avec.

learnerCopy.en: Defuncto Herode means 'when/after Herod had died'. Herode does not perform a role in apparuit; the phrase supplies independent background.
learnerCopy.fr: Defuncto Herode signifie « après la mort d'Hérode / Hérode étant mort ». Herode n'exerce aucune fonction dans apparuit ; le groupe fournit l'arrière-plan.

learnerCopy.en: Convocatis Apostolis means 'having called the Apostles together / when the Apostles had been called'. Both words are ablative plural and form one compressed circumstance.
learnerCopy.fr: Convocatis Apostolis signifie « les Apôtres ayant été convoqués ». Les deux mots sont à l'ablatif pluriel et forment une seule circonstance condensée.

learningBlocks.title: Not every participle is an ablative absolute

learnerCopy.en: Accedentes duodecim is nominative and belongs directly to the main clause subject. Case agreement distinguishes it from an ablative absolute.
learnerCopy.fr: Accedentes duodecim est au nominatif et appartient directement au sujet de la principale. L'accord de cas le distingue d'un ablatif absolu.

learnerCopy.en: Do not identify an ablative absolute merely because a comma appears. Verify ablative agreement and confirm that the phrase's noun is syntactically independent of the main verb.
learnerCopy.fr: N'identifiez pas un ablatif absolu à cause d'une virgule. Vérifiez l'accord à l'ablatif et l'indépendance syntaxique du nom par rapport au verbe principal.

authenticPassages.sourceLatin: Defuncto autem Herode, ecce angelus Domini apparuit in somnis Joseph in Aegypto.
authenticPassages.instructionalDisplay: Defuncto autem Herode, ecce angelus Domini apparuit in somnis Joseph in Aegypto.

translation.en: But when Herod was dead, behold an angel of the Lord appeared in a dream to Joseph in Egypt.
translation.fr: Après la mort d'Hérode, voici qu'un ange du Seigneur apparut en songe à Joseph en Égypte.

authenticPassages.sourceLatin: Convocatis autem duodecim Apostolis, dedit illis virtutem et potestatem super omnia daemonia.
authenticPassages.instructionalDisplay: Convocatis autem duodecim Apostolis, dedit illis virtutem et potestatem super omnia daemonia.

translation.en: And calling together the twelve Apostles, He gave them power and authority over all devils.
translation.fr: Ayant convoqué les douze Apôtres, il leur donna puissance et autorité sur tous les démons.

authenticPassages.sourceLatin: Quod cum cognovissent turbae, secutae sunt illum: et excepit eos, et loquebatur illis de regno Dei.
authenticPassages.instructionalDisplay: Quod cum cognovissent turbae, secutae sunt illum: et excepit eos, et loquebatur illis de regno Dei.

translation.en: Which when the crowds had known, they followed Him; and He received them and spoke to them of the kingdom of God.
translation.fr: Les foules, l'ayant appris, le suivirent ; il les accueillit et leur parlait du royaume de Dieu.

authenticPassages.sourceLatin: Accedentes autem duodecim dixerunt illi: Dimitte turbas.
authenticPassages.instructionalDisplay: Accedentes autem duodecim dixerunt illi: Dimitte turbas.

translation.en: And the twelve coming to Him said: Send away the crowds.
translation.fr: Les douze s'approchèrent et lui dirent : renvoyez les foules.

exercises.hint: Both words are ablative and independent of apparuit.

exercises.prompt: How should Defuncto Herode be understood here?
exercises.explanation: Ablative absolute relation is inferred from context.
